title: House Robber II
keyIdea: The houses are in a circle, so house 0 and house n − 1 can't both be robbed. Any plan leaves out the first house or the last one, so run House Robber on 0..n − 2 and on 1..n − 1 and take the larger. One house: just rob it.

approaches.name: Memoization on two ranges
approaches.idea: Your code: solveUsingMem(start, end) = most money from houses start..end (rob → start + 2, skip → start + 1). Called on 0..n − 2 with dp1 and on 1..n − 1 with dp2.
approaches.why: Each range has at most n − 1 houses, each solved once; two dp arrays of size n plus the recursion stack.

approaches.name: Two variables on each range
approaches.idea: Same two cases, but each one is the House Robber two-variable loop (next1, next2) over its range, right to left.
approaches.why: Two passes over at most n − 1 houses; only two numbers kept per pass.

options: Every valid plan skips the first house or the last, so one of the two runs contains it
3 (houses 0 and 2 are neighbours in the circle)

quiz.q: Why does n == 1 need its own check?
options: Both ranges 0..n − 2 and 1..n − 1 would be empty and give 0

quiz.q: In your memo version, why two dp arrays?
options: The two cases end at different houses, so their saved answers mean different things
One is for odd houses, one for even
